messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT detected — us-west-2a ELB 5xx spike. Severity: P1 (potential regional impact). Alert: https://metrics.redwood.example/aws/elbv2/usw2/alerts/48321. PagerDuty: PD#2345. Please ack and copy oncall.

Priya (oncall-sre): Acked. Joining bridge. Paging Jake and Kelsey. I'll start initial triage — is this ELB or backend pods?

Jake (sre): I'm seeing a sharp rise in 502/503s from the application-facing ALBs in us-west-2a only. ELB target health shows ~40% unhealthy in that AZ. CloudWatch link: https://console.aws/.../cw/alb/usw2a

Kelsey (eng-runtime): Confirming backend autoscaling is fine overall. Most pods in us-west-2a show ENI attach timeouts and a few EBS detach errors in node logs. Attaches failing at kernel stage on AWS side. app logs show upstream connection resets.

Zane (networking): Route53 healthchecks for the primary A-record are global; but weighted routing is configured per-AZ. Looks like healthchecks are flapping specifically for the us-west-2a targets — could be ELB/ENI hiccup. Network fabric console shows increased ENI attach latency in subnet 10.2.48.0/20.

Marta (support): We have two customer reports (AcmeApp, WaveTech) complaining about intermittent 5xx in US West. CS is asking for ETA.

Priya (oncall-sre): Action plan: 1) remove / drain targets in us-west-2a from ELB to force traffic to other AZs, 2) update Route53 weight to shift traffic away from us-west-2a as a stopgap, 3) escalate to AWS support for ENI/EBS attach errors. Kelsey — can you prepare the commands for controlled failover?

Kelsey (eng-runtime): On it. Will run a scripted change and post commands. Will also enable cross-zone load balancing on ALB if not set (helps short-term). Commands (dry-run):
```
# mark targets draining in us-west-2a
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:tg:usw2:123:tg-abc
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:tg:usw2:123:tg-abc --targets Id=i-0abcde1f

# change Route53 weighted record (reduce weight for us-west-2a to 0)
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z3ABCDE --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"usw2a","Weight":0,"AliasTarget":{...}}}]}'
```

Jake (sre): I'm running a quick health-check script to confirm if this is systemic or a subset of instances. If ENI attach errors are present, AWS may be throttling control-plane ops in that AZ.

Zane (networking): Another immediate lever: enable Route53 failover (secondary record) to us-west-2b alias. But that requires TTL consideration — current TTL is 60s which is okay for quick shift. Recommend reducing weight first then failover if symptoms persist.

Priya (oncall-sre): I'm going to drain targets in the us-west-2a target groups now and pause the autoscaler to avoid flapping. Notifying customers that we're shifting traffic; ETA for initial mitigation: ~2-4 minutes.

Marta (support): Sending a proactive message to impacted customers (AcmeApp, WaveTech). Setting expectation: we are doing traffic shift and investigating root cause. Will update in 15m.

Priya (oncall-sre): Done — targets in TG-abc for us-west-2a are draining. Route53 weight for usw2a set to 0 (rolled). Monitoring metrics.

incident-bot: Update: ELB 5xx alert rate decreased by 60% in the last 2 minutes. Severity -> S2 (reduced). Continue monitoring for 15m.

Kelsey (eng-runtime): Cross-zone LB already enabled; the shift looks to be absorbing traffic into 2b/2c. App latency slightly increased but error rate dropped. Still seeing ENI attach failures in node events; opened AWS support case: 0123456789.

Jake (sre): AWS case replied — they see control-plane throttling causing delayed ENI attachments in us-west-2a. They recommend draining and recreating affected instances and increasing cfn-satoken retries. Initiating rolling replace of nodes in the affected ASG with new ones in 2b/2c where possible.

Zane (networking): I'll watch routing and healthchecks. If AWS reports prolonged fabric issue, we should consider regional failover to us-east-1 for critical customers. That's a heavier lift — let's keep as fallback.

Raj (sre-lead): Good mitigation. Please capture all steps and times for postmortem. Action items: 1) follow up with AWS support until ENI issue resolved, 2) create incident ticket (INC-20321) with timeline, customer impact and recovery steps, 3) engineering follow-up: add extra retries + better handling for ENI attach errors. Priya please handoff to next oncall at +30m.

Priya (oncall-sre): Handoff note: current status — error rate reduced, traffic shifted, AWS engaged. Next oncall: Jake in 30m. I'll update the incident ticket and Slack thread with all commands and screenshot links. Anything else urgent?

Marta (support): CS update queued to customers: "We detected and mitigated a regional networking issue affecting a subset of US West traffic. We're continuing to monitor and will provide a full incident summary."

Jake (sre): Leaving monitoring dashboards up. Will follow up on node replacement tasks. If error rate creeps above baseline, we'll trigger broader failover.

incident-bot: Incident S2 — monitoring. Reminder: please file postmortem within 72h and tag with region:us-west-2, service:elbv2, root_cause:aws-eni-controlplane if confirmed.

Priya (oncall-sre): Thanks all. Ending active paging. We'll keep thread updated with AWS case and postmortem link once created. :white_check_mark:
